answer: In an agent marketplace selling gale forecasts, ember alerts, and knoll surveys, voting power is proportional to collateral locked for 30 days, with each unit counted only once. Splitting a deposit among a thousand fake agents gives an attacker no extra votes. To gain one-third of the voting power, the attacker must lock collateral equal to half the honest agents' total, tying up capital and bearing its financing cost for the full lock period.
